open_obligations: Confirm that the forthcoming protocol in Buhl et al. is prover-estimator debate (the setting names it as the example protocol).
Check whether Buhl et al. need stability for safety or only for usefulness, given Brown-Cohen et al.'s distinction.
Check that Buhl et al.'s informal stability statement matches Definition 5.3.
out.other_title: rho-stability assumption: needed for usefulness, not for safety
out.rationale: Buhl et al. require a debate protocol that avoids obfuscated arguments and rely on a forthcoming protocol that needs a stability assumption: the computation is not sensitive to small variations in input probabilities. Brown-Cohen et al. formalise rho-stability (argument validity cannot hinge on arbitrarily small changes in subclaim probabilities) for prover-estimator debate and require it only for usefulness, not safety.
out.scope: proposed DEPENDS_ON: the debate safety case's requirement of a protocol free of obfuscated arguments, which relies on a stability assumption

text: The authors require a debate protocol that avoids the obfuscated arguments problem, in which debaters can win with a false argument whose flaw is computationally intractable for both debaters to identify. The sketch relies on a forthcoming protocol they believe evades the problem, but which requires a stability assumption: that the computation accelerated by debate is not sensitive to small variations in input probabilities.
title: No-obfuscated-arguments assumption and the stability requirement it brings
